title: Operator Safety Net and Incident Judgement Framework
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose
This document defines the operator safety net and an incident judgement framework for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem) to guide on-call operators and field engineers when triaging, containing, and remediating runtime incidents that affect tenant SLAs or data isolation guarantees.

Scope
- Applies to: day-2 operations teams, field operators, SRE rotation covering private deployments.
- Systems covered: runtime control plane, tenant KV cache, model serving fabric, telemetry ingestion gateway, tenant egress proxies.
- Not covered: provisioning CI/CD pipelines and hardware procurement. Those are referenced in related guides.

Principles and goals
1) Fast, evidence-driven judgement: prioritize measurable telemetry over intuition.
2) Contain-first: prefer short automatic mitigations that preserve data safety and service availability before broad rollbacks.
3) Clear escalation and communication: every decision has an owner, an SLA for customer notification, and an entry in the incident log.
4) Reversible actions: prefer actions that are deterministic and reversible (traffic cordon, model-fallback, cache-evict) before destructive changes.

Key signals and where to find them
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 from per-route dashboards (Console -> Private -> Routes -> <route>)
- Error budget and service-level errors: 5xx rate and model inference errors (runtime.metrics.inference_errors)
- KV cache hit ratio: runtime.kv_cache.hit_ratio by tenant
- Tenant memory/GC pressure: host.metrics.mem_free, runtime.metrics.kv_shard_backlog
- Network anomalies: proxy.egress.rtt_ms and proxy.egress.retransmits
- Telemetry ingestion lag: telemetry.queue_depth and telemetry.ingest_latency

Signal thresholds (safety-net table)
| Signal | Warning threshold | Safety-net threshold | Operator action (first 10m) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency (critical routes) | > 500 ms | > 1.5 s for 3 minutes | Activate route-level throttling; enable compact batching profile; notify SRE lead |
| 5xx rate (route) | > 0.5% | > 2% for 2 minutes | Switch traffic to fallback model variant; enable degraded mode; page on-call |
| KV cache hit ratio (tenant) | < 60% | < 40% for 5 minutes | Snapshot KV shard; enable read-through from backing store; reduce concurrency for tenant |
| Telemetry ingest lag | > 30s | > 120s | Pause non-essential telemetry; raise ingestion autoscaler; record evidence for postmortem |
| Host memory free | < 15% | < 7% | Evacuate non-critical pods, throttle tenant bursts, schedule host rebalancing |

Initial triage checklist (first 15 minutes)
1) Confirm alert validity: correlate alert with tracing (trace-id) and recent deploys.
2) Identify blast radius: affected tenants, regions, models, and ingress paths.
3) Take containment actions (see containment section).
4) Start incident log: link customer IDs, dump relevant dashboards and queries.
5) Notify stakeholders per Escalation matrix.

Containment actions (ordered, reversible preferred)
- Step A: Route-level throttling: set per-route qps_limit or token-bucket to reduce tails. CLI example: redwoodctl route throttle set --route-id r123 --qps 50 --duration 30m
- Step B: Model variant fallback: re-route to smaller model version with documented quality delta. redwoodctl model route --from model:v2-large --to model:v2-small --reason "safety-net-fallback"
- Step C: KV cache snapshot + read-through: trigger shard snapshot and set read_through=true for tenant.
- Step D: Tenant grace throttling: apply per-tenant concurrency caps to avoid noisy neighbor.
- Step E: Controlled eviction: evict aged non-critical sessions from host to free memory.

Rollback and rollforward judgement criteria
- Prefer rollforward when: the root cause is fixed in a safe patch, or rollout is staged and can be fast-tracked with automated compatibility checks.
- Prefer rollback when: a recent release/upgrade correlates with incident start time, and the rollback can be completed within the fallout window without state loss.
- Decision checklist before rollback:
  a) Impact window estimate: if rollback will restore >90% of degraded requests within 10 minutes, prefer rollback.
  b) Data-safety assessment: verify that rollback will not corrupt on-disk state or KV snapshots.
  c) Stakeholder approval: for customer-impacting rollbacks, get SRE lead and Platform PM sign-off.

Automated mitigations (pre-configured safety net)
- Canary circuit-breaker: automatically reduce canary traffic by 50% when p95 > 1s for 2 minutes.
- Model degradation policy: automatically swap to quantized variant when host memory pressure > 75%.
- Telemetry backpressure: drop non-critical spans when ingest lag > 60s.

Escalation matrix and communication templates
- Pager (P1): on-call SRE -> SRE lead -> Platform Eng -> CTO. Page immediately when Safety-net threshold exceeded.
- P2: on-call operator -> on-call SRE -> Customer Success manager.
- Customer notification SLA: initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes for P1, 2 hours for P2.

Template: Initial customer acknowledgement (short)
"We are investigating an incident affecting inference performance in your private deployment. Our on-call team has enacted the safety-net mitigation and is working on root cause. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Incident ID: <INC-ID>"

Template: Follow-up update
"Update: mitigation in place (model-fallback). Impact reduced from 35% to 5% of requests failing. Next update within 60 minutes. Owners: SRE (oncall), Field Ops (operator)."

Evidence collection (what to capture before changing state)
- Dashboard snapshots (p50/p95/p99, 5xx rates) for 20 minutes before action.
- Trace examples (3 traces with representative request IDs).
- KV shard status, commit log offsets, and snapshot manifest IDs.
- Runtime process dumps if memory corruption suspected (capture within 2 minutes).

Operator playbook: step-by-step (example P1 scenario)
1) Acknowledge alert and set incident channel in Slack.
2) Run quick diagnostic queries:
   - curl -s "https://console.internal/api/dashboards/route?p95&minutes=20" > /tmp/route_p95.json
   - redwoodctl runtime status --tenant TENANT_ID --output json > /tmp/runtime_status.json
3) Apply containment (Route throttle -> Model fallback). Record all commands in incident log.
4) If containment works (metrics recover to warning thresholds), continue stabilise plan and schedule next steps.
5) If containment fails after 15 minutes, evaluate rollback criteria and coordinate rollback with field operator and CS for customer notice.

Post-incident: judgement review and changelog
- Within 72 hours: short judgement memo describing why the chosen action was taken, comparisons of candidate actions considered, and evidence.
- Within 7 days: full postmortem if incident P1 or if >4 hours customer impact. Postmortem must include reproducible steps and a mitigation timeline.

Operator-run scripts and useful commands
- redwoodctl incident annotate --incident INC-ID --note "Applied model-fallback"
- redwoodctl audit download --tenant TENANT_ID --since "2026-06-01" --until "2026-06-10" > /tmp/audit.json
- redwoodctl model compare --a model:v2-large --b model:v2-small --metrics latency,throughput,mem

Acceptance criteria for safety-net success
- Containment accepted: p95 reduced to < warning threshold and 5xx < 0.5% within 15 minutes.
- Recovery accepted: full restoration of baseline request success rate and KV cache hit within SLA window (24 hours) or documented rollback occurs.

Training and exercises
- Quarterly game-days: simulate model-swap and KV cache corruption scenarios. Operators must complete runbook checklist within target times in a simulated environment.
- Runbook drills: monthly short drills for containment actions using redwoodctl in staging.

References and related guides
- Private deploy commissioning and safety gate playbook (see related_pages).
- Tenant latency regression detection runbook.
- KV cache migrations and runtime state migration playbook.

Appendix: sample alert query (PromQL-like)
- p95 latency (route): quantile_over_time(0.95, latency_ms{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])
- 5xx rate (route): sum(increase(http_requests_total{code=~"5..",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) / sum(increase(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]))
